creator: Alexander Terp
description:
MIP-3 section 8, the step after a_2XJ1gk34C (muster-detect, done) and a_2XJ1gZRTY (pane streams). muster-detect is a pure library; the daemon has to drive it. Per slot 1's round-2 report, the wiring is a timer and two trait implementations:
- `Pane` over the pane's terminal: `foreground_group` (tcgetpgrp on the master, crates/muster-daemon/src/pty.rs), `content_seq` (bumped per non-empty read in the reader), `screen_text` = `Terminal::text(0, rows-1)`, `title` = `Terminal::title()` (the one title the daemon publishes - do not add a second), `progress`/`clear_progress` over a `muster_detect::Progress` fed every chunk in the reader.
- `System` for `Processes`.
- Tick first at `Detector::FIRST_TICK`, then after each `Tick::next`, from the reader's cadence hook slot 2 left; `reset()` and tick when manifests change.
- Publications become the pane's `agent` and `AgentState` on the event stream (the protocol already carries both).
- `session.send_manifests` feeds app-sent manifests into `Manifests::load`; `~/.muster/agent-detection/` overrides; `MUSTER_AGENT` hint. Document both in docs/configuration.md with this change.
Also: run the herdr probe's `detection` scenario (corpus/herdr-0.8.0/detection/) against the new daemon as the migration check, and fold in rich agent state (a_2XMXOShAA) if its design settles in time, since it reads the same screens on the same cadence.
title: Wire muster-detect into muster-daemon: every pane reports its agent and state
